🍎 Lesson plan · 🌱 Basics · Lesson 6

Lesson plan: AI Ethics & Safety

Bias, deepfakes and privacy — and how to use AI responsibly.

By the end of the lesson, students can

  • explain how AI can learn bias from its data, with a real example;
  • check a suspicious video or picture before sharing it;
  • protect their privacy when using AI tools, and explain why people stay responsible for decisions made with AI.

Warm-up

A video shows a famous person saying something shocking. How could you tell whether it is real?

Collect strategies. Point out that looking for glitches gets harder as fakes improve; checking the source works better, which is the lesson's advice.

Reading

Students read the lesson “AI Ethics & Safety”. Students look for the example of the biased hiring tool, and for the lesson's advice on deepfakes and privacy.

Activity: Mini-lab “What would you do?”

  1. Students open the mini-lab in lesson 6 and read the three situations.
  2. For each one, pairs agree on a choice before they click, and note why.
  3. They click their choice and read the feedback; if it wasn't the best choice, they read the better one.
  4. The class votes on which situation is the hardest in real life, and why.

For students who finish early

Fast finishers write a situation of their own, with three choices and the feedback for each.

Discussion questions

  • If an AI learned to be unfair from human decisions, who should fix it, and how?
  • Should AI-made videos always be labelled? Who should make sure they are?
  • Which important decisions should always be checked by a person? Why those?
  • Some families agree on a secret code word for emergency calls. How does that help against voice scams?

Exit ticket

Write one thing you will check before you share a shocking video.

Quick check. A shocking video of a famous person is spreading fast. What is the best way to tell whether it's a deepfake?
Right answer: Check who posted it and whether trusted news reports it

Easier and harder

Easier. Read the situations aloud, and let students vote with A, B and C cards before you discuss each one.

Harder. Students write a short class policy for using AI tools safely: what never to share, how to check AI-made content, and when to say that AI helped.
